chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu 'Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a woman but did not consummate the marriage, and she claimed that her dowry was one hundred dinars, while the man stated it was less than what she said, and she had no proof for her claim, he said: 'The word of the husband is accepted with his oath.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry if the wife claims a higher amount than the husband admits and there is no proof?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the evidentiary standard in pre-consummation dowry disputes, prioritizing the husband's sworn testimony when the wife lacks proof, a ruling distinct from cases where consummation has occurred. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the presumption of truthfulness (qara'in) in financial claims within the marital contract, reflecting the practical legal realities of 9th-century Kufa. The ruling underscores the importance of oaths (yamin) as a decisive legal tool in the absence of written documentation or witnesses.
